experiments.customer: Frozen-food businesses with sudden orders and no logistics (Kuantan)
experiments.problem: Sudden orders they can't refuse but can't deliver
experiments.assumption: They lose sales today because they can't find transport fast

criterion.text: X of Y interviewees describe the pain unprompted (fixed before going out)

experiments.result: Calls: no answer (untested). 3 street interviews: suppliers deliver themselves; real pain = supplier runs out
experiments.learning: The pain we heard was the restaurant's supply, not transport. 2 of 2 is a signal, not proof

customer.text: Halal restaurants and cafes relying on one chicken supplier (Kuantan)

problem.text: Supplier runs out: chicken off the menu or close, can't trust a new supplier

solution.text: Yakin: verified halal backup suppliers nearby (clickable prototype)

experiments.assumption: Owners trust our verification enough to sign up for a backup supplier

criterion.text: At least 3 owners sign up (target 8 visits)

experiments.result: 5 visited, 3 confirmed the problem, tried it and gave contact details
experiments.learning: Sign-up behaviour met the bar on 5 visits. Next risk moves to the supplier side: who pays?
